extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in nonlinear time-series analysis / dynamical systems
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for constructing, interpreting, and quantifying recurrence plots (RPs) and their extensions (CRP, JRP, OPRP, etc.) used in nonlinear time-series and dynamical-systems analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of threshold ε
rubrics_metrics.description: The threshold ε strongly affects the resulting RP structures; dynamical invariants derived from RPs can only be obtained in the limit ε → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ε depends on the system studied. Typical practical choices are finite (often ~10% of mean phase-space radius), but one should be aware that invariants strictly require ε→0. Unthresholded representations or correlation-sum-based Uij can help to find appropriate ε. Using FAN (fixed amount neighbours) yields per-point εi that achieve a fixed recurrence rate RR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale typology: homogeneous RP
rubrics_metrics.description: Homogeneous recurrence plot pattern (uniform point distribution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a stationary process with short relaxation times relative to the RP time span (example: stationary random time series). Useful as a baseline for comparison with other typologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale typology: periodic / quasi-periodic patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagonal-oriented, periodic or quasi-periodic recurrent structures (diagonal lines, checkerboard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cyclicities in the process; distance between diagonal lines corresponds to the period. Rational frequency ratios produce regularly spaced diagonals; irrational ratios produce more complex spacings. Can reveal periodic or unstable periodic orbits even when oscillations are not obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale typology: drift (fading corners)
rubrics_metrics.description: RP fades away from the line of identity toward corners (upper left and lower right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates non-stationary data with slowly varying parameters (a trend or drift). Windowed/meta-RPs are useful to study such non-stationarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale typology: disruptions (white bands)
rubrics_metrics.description: White areas or bands in the RP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests abrupt changes in dynamics, extreme events, rare states, or transitions. RPs allow locating and assessing extreme/rare events via recurrence frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-scale texture: single isolated points
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolated recurrence points scattered in the RP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May indicate rare states, short persistence, or strong fluctuations. If only isolated points occur, the process may be uncorrelated or anti-correlated, but isolated points are not a unique sign of randomness (maps can show isolated points for non-random reasons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-scale texture: diagonal lines parallel to LOI
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagonal lines with slope 1 (parallel to the line of identity) where trajectory segments evolve similarly for l time units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate similar local evolution (determinism); lengths relate to how long segments remain close and connect to dynamical invariants (e.g., Renyi entropy K2, sum of positive Lyapunov exponents). Diagonal lines are the basis for many quantification measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-scale texture: diagonal lines orthogonal to LOI
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagonal structures perpendicular to the LOI (mirrored segments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often hint at inappropriate embedding (segments running in opposite time directions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-scale texture: vertical and horizontal lines / clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical (or horizontal) lines or rectangular clusters of recurrence points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark time intervals where a state does not change or changes very slowly; indicate laminar states or intermittency (state trapping). These structures are central to laminarity-related quantification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-scale texture: bowed (curved) line structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines with non-constant slope (bowed lines) in the RP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect local time-scaling differences between two corresponding trajectory segments; slope b(t) equals the local time derivative of the inverse time-transfer function between segments. Used in CRPs for time-scale alignment and to infer non-parametric rescaling functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude LOI / apply Theiler window
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude the line of identity (and usually a corridor around it) when quantifying RPs to avoid tangential motion effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagonal lines close to the LOI can reflect tangential (self-)motion rather than different orbits. Excluding a corridor (Theiler correction/window w) is recommended for invariant estimation. Suggested choices: Theiler recommended using the auto-correlation time as w, while other authors suggest w = (m−1)τ. Visualising the LOI can also be useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for quantification beyond visual interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual inspection of RPs requires experience and can be subjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantification of RP structures (e.g., measures based on diagonal/vertical lines, recurrence rates, recurrence-time statistics) is necessary for more objective analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frequency considerations / discretization effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling frequency relative to system characteristic frequencies affects RP patterns; if sampling frequency is only one order of magnitude higher and not integer-multiple of system frequencies, recurrences may be missed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretization can produce extended characteristic gaps (white areas) in RPs. Ensure sufficiently high sampling rate (much higher than system frequencies) to avoid aliasing/discretisation artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of embedding on RP structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay embedding (m, τ) can induce spurious correlations and structures (e.g., diagonal lines) in RPs even for uncorrelated noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inappropriate/high embedding dimensions can create spurious long diagonal lines that feign determinism. Embedding parameters must be chosen carefully; alternatively use quantification measures that are embedding-independent. Recognize that R(m) can be constructed from shifted copies of R(1), explaining induced correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neighborhood type: fixed radius vs fixed amount nearest neighbours (FAN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two common neighbourhood criteria: fixed radius ε (symmetric RP) and fixed amount nearest neighbours (FAN) where εi varies per point (asymmetric RP with constant column recurrence density).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which neighbourhood to use depends on the purpose. FAN ensures a constant recurrence density (RR) and is especially useful for cross recurrence plots and detection of generalized synchronisation. Fixed radius is most common and yields symmetric RPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance / unthresholded / correlation-sum based representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of thresholding, plot distances Di,j or correlation-sum-based Ui,j (unthresholded recurrence plots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These representations (distance plot, unthresholded RP, Ui,j from C2) can help study phase-space geometry and assist in selecting an appropriate ε. Applying a threshold to Ui,j yields RPs with exact recurrence density ε.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corridor threshold [ε_in, ε_out]
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a shell neighbourhood where recurrences are those points whose distance lies between ε_in and ε_out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increases robustness against tangential-motion-induced recurrences, but removes inner points of broad diagonal lines producing two lines instead of one—thus not directly suitable for quantification analysis. Has been used in attempts to compute Lyapunov exponents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpendicular recurrence plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Define recurrence using distances perpendicular to the phase-space trajectory (Poincaré-like section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleans RP more effectively from tangential-motion false recurrences than corridor threshold; more efficient for estimating invariants and detecting unstable periodic orbits (UPOs). Recommended for quantification based on diagonal structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iso-directional recurrence plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines recurrences among neighbouring trajectories that run parallel and in the same direction (adds a directional constraint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleaner than common RP but less effective than perpendicular RP. Simpler to compute than perpendicular RP but requires an additional parameter T (which may relate to embedding delay τ) that must be determined carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-return / close-returns / projected RPs (non-square / time-distance RPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test each state with a predefined amount k of subsequent states (non-square RP) or project diagonals to horizontal axis (close-returns plot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Y-axis represents time distances to following recurrences rather than absolute time; useful/ intuitive for detecting periodic orbits and first-return statistics. Forms basis for recurrence-time histograms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Windowed and meta recurrence plots for non-stationarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Windowed RPs average recurrence points in w-sized squares producing an N_w x N_w matrix with values corresponding to cross-correlation sums; meta-RP is a distance matrix derived from cross-correlation sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Windowed RPs are useful for detecting transitions and long-range patterns in very long data series (colour-encoded values). Meta-RP (and thresholded versions) and meta phase-space constructions (Manuca & Savit) can characterise non-stationarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order patterns recurrence plot (OPRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define recurrence by equality of local ordinal patterns π of dimension d (symbolisation by ranks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust to non-stationary data and increases applicability of cross recurrence plots; useful when absolute amplitudes differ or slow drifts are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinal / hybrid (ordinal+closeness) recurrence plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid that requires both spatial closeness and matching sign of local growth/shrink (ordinal cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines proximity and simultaneous increasing/decreasing behaviour; adds robustness in detecting meaningful recurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'recurrent plots' is sometimes used in literature but is not recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the established term 'recurrence plots' (RP) and be aware certain other uses of 'recurrence plots' in unrelated contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of RP definition depends on analysis goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the RP variant according to the problem, system/data characteristics, and intended quantification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perpendicular RPs are recommended for diagonal-structure-based quantification; corridor-thresholded RPs are unsuitable for such quantification; windowed RPs for long-range visualization; horizontal-LOI RPs when interest is in recurrences following a pre-defined time offset. The report uses the standard RP definition per [2].

rubrics_metrics.name: CRP requirement: shared phase space / normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross recurrence plots (CRPs) compare states of two systems and require both trajectories to be represented in the same phase space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When embedding experimental data, if embedding parameters differ choose the higher embedding. Components are usually normalised before computing CR matrix. Exceptions: order-pattern CRP allows different observables/amplitudes because it compares rank sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRP interpretation: diagonal lines and similarity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagonally oriented lines in a CRP represent trajectory segments from both systems that run parallel for some time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequency and length of diagonal lines relate to the similarity between dynamics; measures based on these lines can detect nonlinear interrelations not found by linear cross-correlation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRP utility: local time-scaling and LOS extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Bowed or distorted line of synchronisation (LOS) in CRP reflects time-dilatation/compression between trajectories (time-transfer function).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LOS can be resolved to obtain a non-parametric rescaling function t = φ(t') aligning two series. A time shift dislocates LOS; identical trajectories produce LOI (main diagonal). Useful for time-scale alignment (e.g., sediment compression examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: CRP practical neighbourhood choices for robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Using FAN or order-pattern neighbourhoods in CRP can avoid normalization and work well for slowly changing trajectories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAN yields constant recurrence density and is robust under drift; order-pattern CRP is robust to non-stationarity and amplitude differences.
